data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate opened 2021 with gross claims outstanding of 2,840.1 (USD millions). During 2021 it recorded a prior-year release of $105.2m (favourable development), primarily driven by development in the Treaty, Marine and Energy divisions. The release equates to approximately a 3.7% reduction on opening gross reserves. The reserve movement is attributed to favourable claims development on prior year losses; the syndicate remains exposed to prior-year events including Covid-19 (estimated gross $215.4m) and 2020 hurricanes such as Laura and Sally (combined gross estimates noted), which are disclosed in the technical reserves note.
raw_causal_phrases: During 2021 the Syndicate released $105.2m of technical reserves in respect of prior periods (2020: $74.5m), arising predominantly from the Treaty, Marine and Energy divisions (2020: predominantly from the Marine, Energy and Treaty divisions).
These releases were due to favourable claims development on prior year losses during 2021.

The Syndicate has exposure to losses emanating from the Covid-19 pandemic and the ensuing Global Economic Crisis. The current estimated ultimate claims are $215.4m gross and $132.6m net of reinsurance. After inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums this reduces to $132.0m.

The Syndicate also has exposure to a number of natural catastrophe events that occurred in 2020. The largest of these are hurricanes Laura and Sally. The current estimated ultimate claims for these events are $49.9m gross and $37.9m net of reinsurance. After inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums this reduces to $33.3m.

data.data_quality_notes: Primary prior-year movement sourced from the 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' narrative which explicitly states a $105.2m release (assumed gross). Opening gross claims outstanding taken from the Statement of Financial Position (claims outstanding prior year comparative). A gross claims development triangle is present; an RITC was accepted effective 1 January 2022 (post year-end) and a Part VII reclassification is noted, but no RITC within 2021 that would materially distort the 2021 triangle was identified. Where LOB-level allocations of the prior year release are not provided, LOB assignments are left null and confidence reduced accordingly.
